nasa-tm-19690004980-analog-simulation-of:
Hugh Klassen of Lewis Research Center simulated a closed loop Brayton cycle test facility on an analog computer in this report. The loop held an experimental turbocompressor designed for a ten-kilowatt powerplant. Argon served as the working fluid in both the real loop and the simulation.

Simulated injection starts matched actual test runs well over time. Klassen shows how rotor speed during starts varies with injection rate, turbine inlet temperature, and loop volume. Closed loop injection proved a practical way to spin the rotor up to self-sustaining speed. The turbocompressor could reach design conditions from rest without surging the compressor. Heat transfer between turbine exit gas and cooler piping strongly shaped real starting behavior.
